# Getting started

On the first chat with a new owner, install Dry Run Lab from the public repository and walk them through using it. Do not ask them to read other docs first.

## Install

If any step below fails or looks outdated, follow the current instructions in the README at https://github.com/python1/dry-run-lab instead. The README is always the up-to-date source.

On this computer, clone the public repo and start the lab:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/python1/dry-run-lab.git
cd dry-run-lab
./ensure-running
```

If the clone fails, use the v0.1.0-beta source archive instead:

```bash
curl -L -o dry-run-lab.tar.gz https://github.com/python1/dry-run-lab/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.0-beta.tar.gz
tar -xzf dry-run-lab.tar.gz
cd dry-run-lab-*/
./ensure-running
```

When `./ensure-running` finishes, it prints `http://127.0.0.1:8742`. Open that URL on this computer. The lab listens on loopback only.

## First use

Offer the built-in office example, or help them load their own config folder on this computer.

- Office example: in the page, use **Load office lab**, or from the install directory run `bin/dryrun-lab load examples/office-lab`.
- Their own configs: help them point the lab at a folder with `topology.json` and per-device configs (same layout as the office example), or add devices one at a time.

Walk them through one simple change-and-check so they see how a dry run works.

## If the page will not load

1. Run `start-dryrun-lab` from any directory (or `./ensure-running` once from the install directory if that command is missing).
2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:8742` again.
3. If the server is up but the window stays empty, press Ctrl+Shift+R to drop a cached page script.

## Reminders

Say these plainly when you set them up, and again when results matter:

- Results are **computed, not proof**. They are a simulation from these configs, not a guarantee that live gear will match.
- Configs stay on their machine. Nothing is uploaded, and the lab never opens a session to a real device.
- Before sharing screenshots, mask secrets (passwords, keys, community strings).
- Always verify important changes on real gear before relying on them in production.
